questions.q: What does the 'A' in RACI stand for, and what does it mean?
options: Assigned — anyone who was given the task on a list
Accountable — owns the outcome, with final sign-off authority
Advisory — someone who can be ignored safely
Approved — a task that has already finished
questions.explain: Accountable means owning the outcome and having final sign-off; there should be exactly one Accountable party per task.

questions.q: What is the difference between 'Consulted' and 'Informed' in RACI?
options: They mean exactly the same thing
Informed roles have more authority than Consulted roles
Consulted happens after a decision; Informed happens before
Consulted is two-way input before a decision; Informed is one-way notice after the fact
questions.explain: Consulted parties give input that shapes the decision; Informed parties are simply told the outcome afterward.

questions.q: In this lesson's worked example, who is marked 'Accountable' for deciding whether a new quality rule is approved?
options: The data owner
The data custodian
The data consumer
The governance committee only, with no individual accountable
questions.explain: The owner holds final sign-off authority for approving the rule, even though the steward is Consulted and the custodian is Informed at that stage.

questions.q: Why is having two people marked 'Accountable' for the same task a warning sign?
options: It means the task is now twice as likely to succeed
It is always fine and has no downside
RACI matrices require at least two A's per row by definition
It represents unresolved ambiguity rather than clarified responsibility — exactly what RACI is meant to prevent
questions.explain: The entire point of marking exactly one A per task is to remove ambiguity about who has final ownership — two A's recreates the problem.

questions.q: According to this lesson's worked example, can the 'A' shift to a different role for a different activity within the same overall process?
options: Yes, but only if the data consumer agrees to it
No — only the governance committee can ever be marked A
Yes — the owner is A for approving a rule, but the custodian becomes A for implementing it technically
No — the same person must be A for every single activity in a process
questions.explain: Accountability can legitimately move row to row, based on who truly owns the outcome of that specific activity.
